world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Hildebrandt, Kristine A. & Perry, J. Joseph. 2011. Preliminary notes on Gyalsumdo, an undocumented Tibetan variety in Manang District, Nepal.

sources.citation: Tournadre, Nicolas & Hiroyuki Suzuki. 2023. The Tibetic Languages: An Introduction to the Family of Languages Derived from Old Tibetan. Paris: LACITO. Sec. 7.3.3 'Stress' (pp. 241-242), 7.3.4 'Prosodic patterns' (pp. 242-243), p. 576 n. 51
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Family-level only: 'The distinction of stress is attested mainly in Balti'; tonal dialects have a trochaic (strong-weak) pattern on the first two syllables. Nubri and Gyalsumdo appear only in the Kyirong-Yolmo classification (p. 576 with n. 51 citing Hildebrandt & Perry 2011); no Nubri- or Gyalsumdo-specific stress statement.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page nubr1241 (Gyalsumdo-Nubri); dialects Gyalsumdo [gyal1236], Nubri [nubr1243] with Lho, Namrung, Prok, Sama [sama1294]
sources.note: Bibliographic only; lists Hildebrandt & Perry 2011 for subclassification.

sources.citation: Hildebrandt, Kristine A. & J. Joseph Perry. 2011. Preliminary notes on Gyalsumdo, an undocumented Tibetan variety in Manang District, Nepal. Himalayan Linguistics 10(1): 167-185. DOI 10.5070/H910123573
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online (also online with a university library login)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent. Sec. 4 (pp. 172-178) is an acoustic study of the reflexes of the four Central Tibetan tone/register series in 50 obstruent-initial words from one speaker; p. 174 states measurements used only the initial syllable 'under the assumption that more patterns and contrasts are located on the initial syllable of disyllabics', as in Kyirong (Huber 2002). Appendix marks perceived relative pitch (ā high, a low), not stress.

sources.citation: Donohue, Cathryn & Mark Donohue. 2023. The vowels of Nubri from the perspective of other Tibetan languages. Nepalese Linguistics 37(1): 10-18. DOI 10.3126/nl.v37i1.60008
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Nine oral vowels plus contrastive nasalisation on three; length, breathiness and creak treated as functions of the tonal contrasts.

sources.citation: Donohue, Cathryn & Mark Donohue. 2019. The complexity of tone in Nubri. Nepalese Linguistics 34: 18-25. DOI 10.3126/nl.v34i1.41161
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent on stress (the word occurs only in the title of the cited Caplow 2009 dissertation). Describes Sama(gaun) Nubri as having five contrastive tones on monosyllables (H 44, HM 53, M 33, ML 21, LML 231; low tones breathy) and the same five contrasts preserved on disyllables, with restricted tonal combinations.
